papers.title_in_file: Evaluating the performance of sigmoid quantum perceptrons in quantum neural networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section II expressibility discussion, unitary-learning results, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study comparing sigmoid quantum perceptron networks with simpler parameterized circuits on expressibility and learning tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that simpler parameterized quantum circuits perform better than networks of sigmoid quantum perceptrons, and conclude that the universal approximation theorem is not a relevant criterion for quantum neural networks.
quotes: This indicates that the universal approximation theorem, which a cornerstone of the theory of classical neural networks, is not a relevant criterion for QNNs.
However, the numerical data presented in this paper does not support that hope.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation results from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: A negative result for one QNN design family; it does not show that no quantum perceptron design helps.

assertions.value: The authors report that the sigmoid quantum perceptron network was unable to approximate the target unitary across a wide range of hyperparameters and initializations.
quotes: This network was unable to approximate the target unitary, even for a wide range of hyperparameters and intialisations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single numerical experiment reported in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that their work does not conclusively rule out use cases for sigmoid quantum perceptrons, and that assessing larger networks is beyond the scope of the manuscript.
quotes: This work does not conclusively rule out the possibility of use-cases for SQPs.
such an assessment is beyond the scope of this manuscript.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limit in the Conclusion, p.9.

papers.title_in_file: Maximum-Likelihood-Estimate Hamiltonian learning via efficient and robust quantum likelihood gradient
papers.version_note: File name carries the v1 title (Supervised Hamiltonian learning via efficient and robust quantum descent); the file text is arXiv 2212.13718v2 with the record's title. Same paper.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, theorem statement and proof outline, section V discussions
papers.what_it_is: A maximum-likelihood Hamiltonian learning protocol for quantum many-body systems using a quantum likelihood gradient, with a proof of monotone descent and numerical examples.

assertions.value: The authors prove that the quantum likelihood gradient is negative semi-definite with respect to the negative-log-likelihood function.
assertions.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Section II theorem and proof
quotes: which we prove is negative semi-definite with respect to the negative-log-likelihood function
We have theoretically proved the efficiency and convergence of the corresponding quantum likelihood gradient
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem in Section II with proof (Appendix D for the eigenstate case).

assertions.value: The authors report that their protocol shows better accuracy, better robustness against noise and less temperature dependence than previous approaches, demonstrated on multiple examples.
quotes: Compared with previous approaches, it also exhibits better accuracy and overall stability toward noises, fluctuations, and temperature ranges, which we demonstrate with various examples.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical demonstrations on chosen examples.
assertions.reader_inference: No ML workload; Hamiltonian learning for quantum systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that the protocol applies to any Hamiltonian, but its advantages are most apparent for local Hamiltonians.
quotes: its advantages are most apparent for local Hamiltonians
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of scope and limitation in Section V.

papers.title_in_file: Toward Quantum Machine Translation of Syntactically Distinct Languages
papers.what_it_is: A small-scale quantum NLP study of English to Persian translation using parameterized circuits with Shannon entropy and an LSTM encoder-decoder.

assertions.value: The authors report training on a small dataset of English sentences and Persian translations and obtaining a mean absolute error of 0.03, a mean squared error of 0.002 and 0.016 loss with their best model.
quotes: Our experiments involved 160 samples comprising English sentences and their Persian translations.
with mean absolute error of 0.03, mean squared error of 0.002, and 0.016 loss
assertions.certainty_reason: Single small-scale experiment reported in the abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: Error figures are on a 160-sample, word-to-word dataset; no classical baseline comparison is given in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that their dataset is small and consists of simple synonymous sentences with word-to-word mappings.
quotes: Our small dataset, though consisting of simple synonymous sentences with word-to-word mappings
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of the setup and its limits in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum neural machine translation could offer advantages over classical methods in the future, and that more complex models may be needed for intricate sentence structures.
quotes: However, we recognize that more complex machine translation models may be necessary to handle more intricate sentence structures.
which could offer advantages over classical methods in the future.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author expectation, not shown in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Neural Networks: A Comparative Analysis and Noise Robustness Evaluation
papers.what_it_is: A simulation comparison of three hybrid quantum neural network types (QCNN, QuanNN, QTL) for image classification, then under five quantum noise channels.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Quanvolutional Neural Network is, in most scenarios, more robust across the quantum noise channels tested and consistently outperforms the other models.
quotes: However, in most scenarios, the QuanNN demonstrates greater robustness across various quantum noise channels, consistently outperforming other models.
Our findings reveal that QuanNN consistently outperforms other models across different types of quantum noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on image classification tasks.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract hedges with 'in most scenarios'; the conclusion drops the hedge.

assertions.value: The authors report that the top-performing models exhibit varying resilience to different noise gates, so model choice should be tailored to the noise environment.
quotes: Our results reveal that the top-performing models exhibit varying resilience to different noise gates.
This highlights the importance of tailoring model selection to specific noise environments in NISQ devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given the limits of current NISQ devices, the QCNN can only handle a small number of qubits, which limits its scalability, so classical layers reduce large inputs.
quotes: However, given the limitations of current NISQ devices, the QCNN can only handle a small number of qubits, limiting its scalability.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of a limit of the setup they study.

papers.title_in_file: A survey on the complexity of learning quantum states
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section 2 (tomography) theorem statements, section 5 quantum PAC statements, section 6 closing open questions
papers.what_it_is: A survey of rigorous results on the sample and time complexity of learning quantum states, with 25 open questions.

assertions.value: The authors state that learning an arbitrary n-qubit quantum state has a sample complexity known to be exponential in n.
quotes: Given the generality of this task, the sample complexity of this task is known to be exponential in n.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey restating results from other work; not a new result.

assertions.value: The survey states, citing Haah et al. and O'Donnell and Wright, that quantum state tomography up to a given trace distance has an optimal sample complexity stated in its Theorem 1.
quotes: Two breakthrough works by Haah et al. [HHJ+17] and O'Donnell and Wright [OW16] finally obtained optimal bounds for the sample complexity of QST.
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited result; the survey sketches but does not originate the proof.

assertions.value: The survey states, citing Arunachalam and de Wolf, that in distribution-independent PAC and agnostic learning, quantum sample complexity equals classical sample complexity up to constant factors.
quotes: showed that quantum sample complexity of learning is equal to classical sample complexity of
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited result.
assertions.reader_inference: Bears on whether quantum examples give a sample advantage for learning classical functions.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum-Assisted Vehicle Routing: Realizing QAOA-based Approach on Gate-Based Quantum Computer
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, experimental results section 4, limitations 4.6, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A hardware demonstration of QAOA for the vehicle routing problem on IBM Quantum System One, on very small instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the small three-node, two-vehicle instance QAOA generated a feasible routing configuration.
quotes: demonstrating that QAOA was able to generate a feasible routing configuration.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single small instance run on hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: Only a tiny instance; result does not show a quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors report that a four-node problem took over two hours to run on the quantum computer and gave an infeasible solution, with the ten most sampled states all infeasible.
quotes: This problem took over 2 hours to run on the quantum computer and generated an infeasible solution.
In fact, the top 10 most sampled states were all infeasible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single hardware run reported in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that scalability remains constrained by circuit complexity and decoherence.
quotes: While scalability remains constrained by circuit complexity and decoherence
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of the limit of the study in the abstract.

papers.title_in_file: Can Entanglement-enhanced Quantum Kernels Improve Data Classification?
papers.what_it_is: A small-scale quantum SVM kernel study on respiratory sensor data and standard datasets, claiming higher accuracy than classical SVM.

assertions.value: The authors report that their quantum SVM reaches higher accuracy than classical algorithms on complex respiratory data, by 45%, on a 2-qubit system, with comparable performance on linear datasets.
quotes: Compared to classical algorithms, our findings reveal that QSVM performs better with higher accuracy 45% for complex respiratory data sets while maintaining comparable performance with linear datasets in contrast to their classical counterparts executed on a 2-qubit system.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the paper also calls the same figure both accuracy and precision.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract and body use '45%' for both accuracy and precision, and it is unclear whether it is a relative or absolute gain. The paper's own attribution of the gain to entanglement is not isolated by an ablation in the text I read.

assertions.value: The authors attribute the higher accuracy of the quantum SVM to entangled quantum states mapping data to a much higher-dimensional space.
quotes: The higher accuracy of the quantum SVM is attributed to the entangled quantum states effectively mapping data to a much higher-dimensional space compared to classical or nonentangled quantum mappings
assertions.certainty_reason: Explanation asserted by the authors without a separate test in the quoted passage.

papers.title_in_file: One particle - one qubit: Particle physics data encoding for quantum machine learning
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2502.17301v2, published in Physical Review D 112 (2025) 076004.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, encoding, results on QAE and VQC, summary
papers.what_it_is: A data encoding scheme assigning one qubit per particle for collider jet data, tested with a quantum autoencoder and a variational classifier in simulation, plus CMS data.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum autoencoder beats the classical autoencoder across all signal types while using only 31 trainable parameters.
quotes: The QAE achieves superior performance compared to the CAE across all signal types.
The QAE maintains this advantage despite having only 31 trainable parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, in simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is to one classical autoencoder design, not a tuned classical benchmark set.

assertions.value: The authors report that the variational quantum classifier approaches the performance of state-of-the-art classical models with a minimal parameter count.
quotes: the VQC exhibits strong classification capability, approaching the performance of state-of-theart classical models despite its minimal parameter count.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; a small-sample comparison against ParT.
assertions.reader_inference: Approaching, not matching: the paper's own table has the classical model slightly ahead.

assertions.value: The authors state that they limit the study to jet substructure rather than whole events, and use up to ten of the hardest constituents, because of the limits of current quantum computers and their simulators.
quotes: we limit our studies to the intrinsic structure of jets rather than entire events due to the limitations of currently available quantum computers and their simulators.
we limit our study by using up to ten hardest jet constituents
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of the study's scope and limit.
